changedBeliefs: Exp 018/074's multi-row read prototypes were confounded by copying transient TEXT/BLOB payloads into a side arena. Exp 224 tested the remaining pure-numeric frontier without that copy: batch contiguous INTEGER/FLOAT/NULL rows dynamically, but return immediately after a pointer-backed row so Dart decodes SQLite-owned bytes before the next step.

Collapsing a 10,000-row numeric scan from roughly 10,001 leaf FFI calls to about 157 does not improve end-to-end `select()`: 10k x 8 INTEGER is +1.9% / +0.5% candidate-slower across the order flip, while 10k x 20 INTEGER flips +4.6% / -0.5% around zero.

The no-copy TEXT guard path still reproduces a material regression (+6.5% / +5.3% on 10k x 20 short TEXT). The integrated batch-shaped decoder costs more than the removed leaf crossings on current Dart/SQLite baselines; this A/B does not isolate the relative shares of its larger buffer, row-major indexing, stop flag, and shared Dart batch loop.
nextSignals: Do not retry multi-row `select()` stepping with another batch size, copied payload arena, or declared-type shortcut under the current runtime. Exp 018/074 close the copy forms, exp 200 closes hidden storage-class stability, and exp 224 closes the dynamic no-copy numeric-run form.

Reopen only if a Dart runtime change makes leaf FFI crossings materially more expensive, or a production/AOT profile identifies the crossing itself rather than SQLite stepping, per-cell dispatch, or Dart allocation as a top rows-path cost.

Keep `benchmark/experiments/select_rows_step_row_ffi.dart` as the durable rows-path gate: INTEGER lanes are the batching target, while short-TEXT and mixed lanes must guard the direct borrowed-pointer path.
